nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis and calcination
nodes.procedure: NiO@NiCo₂O₄ was obtained via hydrothermal reaction and subsequent calcination process: During the hydrothermal reaction, elemental Ni has a nonuniform distribution and will be enriched on the surfaces of the mix metal hydroxide precursors. After the subsequent calcination process, NiO clusters are formed on the surface of NiCo₂O₄ nanoflakes, which is confirmed by the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

properties.description: Dense mat of nanofibers with fibrous morphology

nodes.source_text: the HER activity of the Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ on graphene/Ni foam sample was evaluated in a H₂-saturated 1 m potassium hydroxide (KOH) electrolyte using a typical three-electrode cell at room temperature... it exhibits good catalytic activity with a low onset potential of about -15 mV, the overpotential is 27 mV at the current density of 10 mA cm⁻² with a Tafel slope of 27 mV dec⁻¹... nearly no difference can be observed between the curves measured at the initial cycle and after 4000 cyclic voltammetry cycles... only shows a slight anodic current attenuation of 2.56% after 45 h... gives ≈100% Faradaic yield with the HER current of 100 mA cm⁻²

The electrocatalytic OER performances were evaluated using a typical three-electrode system in O₂-saturated 1.0 M KOH aqueous electrolyte... more negative OER onset potential (1.50 V)... small Tafel slope (27.9 mV dec⁻¹)... only a little anodic current loss is observed after 1000 continuous cycles... maintain good catalytic activity for at least 20 h
two pieces of Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ were applied as the cathode and the anode for electrocatalytic overall water splitting... achieved 100 mA cm⁻² at 1.65 V with a Tafel slope of 66 mV dec⁻¹
The results of linear sweep voltammograms (LSV) of Pt/C... shows very high electrocatalytic activity with the onset potential nearly 0 mV
for Ni₅P₄, onset potential is about -40 mV and the overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² was about 100 mV with a Tafel slope of 80.4 mV dec⁻¹
for NiCo₂O₄, onset potential is about -100 mV and the overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² was about 125 mV with a Tafel slope of 91.4 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniformly distributed Ni5P4@NiCo2O4 nanoflakes on graphene/Ni foam with flake-like structures of lateral length ≈1 μm and thickness about 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1. a) SEM image showing the uniformly distributed Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ nanoflakes on graphene/Ni foam. b) High-magnification SEM image of Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ nanoflakes.

properties.features: nanofibers, fibrous network, high surface area morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-magnification TEM confirms flake-like structures of Ni5P4@NiCo2O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1c confirms the flake-like structures of the Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows nanometric Ni5P4 clusters nested on NiCo2O4 nanoflakes with (111) plane of NiCo2O4 and (004), (103) facets of Ni5P4 nanoclusters of tens of nm size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: e) High-resolution TEM image showing that nanometric Ni₅P₄ clusters are nested on the nanoflakes. f) HRTEM image of one single Ni₅P₄ nanocluster.

properties.description: HR-TEM or HR-SEM showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of Ni, Co, O, and P elements over Ni5P4@NiCo2O4 nanoflakes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: d) corresponding energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images of Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ nanoflakes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows O 1s peaks at 529.2 eV (metal-oxygen), Ni 2p (Ni²⁺ at 855.1 eV, Ni³⁺ at 856.2 eV), Co 2p (Co²⁺ and Co³⁺), P 2p at 129.1/130.5 eV (metal phosphides) and 135 eV (P⁵⁺ phosphate).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2. XPS profiles of the a) O 1s peak, b) Ni 2p peak, c) Co 2p peak and d) P 2p peak of Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show both Ni5P4 and NiCo2O4 phases exist in Ni5P4@NiCo2O4 sample with no extraneous peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns for Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ on graphene/Ni foam... which demonstrates that both the patterns of Ni₅P₄ and NiCo₂O₄ exist in the Ni₅P₄@NiCo₂O₄ on graphene/Ni foam sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of Ni5P4@NiCo2O4 nanoflakes mainly corresponds to NiCo2O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inset of (c) is the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the nanoflakes, which is mainly corresponding to NiCo₂O₄.
